angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 786,141 km at 63.86 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.6585 +/- 0.0232 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 63.86 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.13 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Murgas et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 20329 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...668A.158M/abstract): 786,141 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Murgas et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 20329 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...668A.158M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5596 +/- 50 K from Murgas et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 20329 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...668A.158M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Murgas et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 20329 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...668A.158M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-20329.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.286, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
